name: CMake unity (jumbo) builds
listed_description: CMake feature (UNITY_BUILD property, CMAKE_UNITY_BUILD variable, batch size 8 by default, UNITY_GROUP) that merges several source files into one translation unit through #include to cut compile time and widen cross-file optimization.
listed_license: BSD-3-Clause (not stated in the chunk; confirmed on the GitHub mirror page)
claim_text: Tests on Qt Creator show an improvement anywhere between 20% to 50%, depending on the compiler used.
book_benchmark: No benchmark run by the book; it cites third-party Qt Creator tests (via a Qt blog link in Further reading) with no workload, compiler version, flags or CPU stated. Book also warns of lost parallelism, higher memory use, symbol collisions in anonymous namespaces and worse incremental rebuilds.
found_in: book: Modern CMake for C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7 Compiling C++ Sources with CMake, section Reducing compilation time / Unity builds

name: CMake precompiled headers (target_precompile_headers)
listed_description: CMake 3.16 command that compiles listed headers once into a compiler-specific .pch/.gch file per target (REUSE_FROM shares it between targets) to speed up compilation.
listed_license: BSD-3-Clause (not stated in the chunk; confirmed on the GitHub mirror page)
claim_text: Allows the compiler to process headers separately from the implementation file, thereby speeding up the compilation process (no numbers given).
book_benchmark: No measurement. Companion example is ch07/06-precompile in the Packt repository https://github.com/PacktPublishing/Modern-CMake-for-Cpp-2E (precompiles <iostream> for a hello-world); it carries no timings.
guessed_baseline: plain #include of the same headers in every translation unit
found_in: book: Modern CMake for C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7 Compiling C++ Sources with CMake, section Reducing compilation time / Precompilation of headers

name: C++20 modules with CMake 3.28 (Ninja 1.11+)
listed_description: Native C++20 module support in CMake (experimental in 3.26, official in 3.28) using binary module interfaces so importers avoid reparsing headers; needs Ninja 1.11+ and a recent Clang, GCC or MSVC.
listed_license: BSD-3-Clause (not stated in the chunk; confirmed on the GitHub mirror page)
claim_text: Modules were introduced to reduce compilation time; the binary module interface significantly reduces recompilation needed by consumers (no numbers given).
book_benchmark: No measurement. Companion examples are in ch10 of https://github.com/PacktPublishing/Modern-CMake-for-Cpp-2E (a math module returning a sum of two ints); the book itself says module support is early and not for production.
guessed_baseline: header-based builds with repeated header parsing per translation unit
found_in: book: Modern CMake for C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 10 Using the C++20 Modules, section What are the C++20 modules?
